plants.name: Japanese Maple (Red Laceleaf)
plants.watering: Water during 10+ day dry spells. Not drought tolerant when young.
plants.fertilizing: Light balanced fertilizer in spring only. Less is more.
plants.pruning: Late winter only — remove dead or crossing branches. Minimal intervention.

seasonal.spring: Watch for rootstock green shoots — remove immediately at the base.
seasonal.summer: Monitor for stress. Remove any green rootstock shoots monthly Apr-Sep.
seasonal.winter: Prune if needed in late winter while dormant.

warnings: Front yard specimen has a rootstock issue — inspect monthly April through September and remove ALL green shoots from the base immediately. The rootstock will overtake the desirable purple variety if not controlled.
Never prune in summer — risk of bleeding and stress.
plants.notes: Two specimens on property — front yard (rootstock issue documented) and back yard.

plants.name: Annabelle Hydrangea
plants.watering: Water deeply during summer. Wilts dramatically in heat — this is normal but water if wilting persists into evening.
plants.pruning: Cut back HARD to 12-18 inches in late February or March. Blooms on NEW wood so aggressive pruning = more blooms.

seasonal.summer: Blooms July-August. May need staking when in full bloom. Water during heat.
seasonal.fall: Leave seed heads for winter interest. Do not prune.
seasonal.winter: Prune late Feb/early March before new growth.

warnings: Wilts dramatically in afternoon heat — this looks alarming but is usually fine. Check in the evening; if still wilted, water deeply.
May need staking when in full bloom as flower heads are heavy.

plants.name: Bigleaf Hydrangea
plants.watering: Water 3x per week in summer. Afternoon shade helps. Most water-demanding hydrangea.
plants.fertilizing: Acidic fertilizer (Espoma HollyTone or similar). Soil pH 5.5-6.5 for blue blooms; pH 6.5+ turns blooms pink.
plants.pruning: ONLY prune immediately after summer blooming finishes. NEVER in fall, winter, or spring — blooms on OLD wood and pruning at wrong time eliminates next year's flowers.

seasonal.spring: DO NOT PRUNE. Buds are forming on old wood. Fertilize.
seasonal.summer: Blooms. Prune only after flowers fade.

warnings: CRITICAL: Blooms only on OLD wood. Pruning at ANY time other than immediately after summer bloom will eliminate next year's flowers entirely.
Most commonly killed by well-meaning pruning in fall or spring.

plants.name: Double Knockout Rose
plants.watering: Regular watering. Drip irrigation ideal. Avoid wetting foliage.
plants.fertilizing: Rose-specific fertilizer (Espoma Rose-tone) every 4-6 weeks spring through August. Stop fertilizing by August 15.
plants.pruning: Late February or early March — cut back by about 1/3. Remove any dead or crossing canes.

seasonal.spring: Prune late Feb/March. Apply fertilizer as new growth emerges.
seasonal.summer: Deadhead spent blooms for continuous reblooming. Watch for Japanese beetles June-July.

warnings: Japanese beetles are a serious pest June through July. Handpick in early morning when they're sluggish, or use neem oil spray. Avoid Japanese beetle traps — they attract more than they catch.
Black spot fungal disease — treat with fungicide if spotted; improve air circulation.

plants.name: Azalea (Robin Hill type)
plants.watering: Moderate, consistent moisture. Good drainage essential. Shallow roots — mulch heavily.
plants.fertilizing: Acidic fertilizer (HollyTone) in spring, right after blooming.
plants.pruning: ONLY within 3 weeks of bloom finishing in spring. NEVER prune in fall or late summer.

seasonal.spring: Blooms April-May. Prune within 3 weeks of bloom end if needed.
seasonal.summer: Leave alone. Buds forming for next year.

warnings: Pruning window is critical: only within 3 weeks of the last bloom in spring. After that, next year's buds begin forming on old wood.
Soil pH must be 4.5-6.0. Test soil if blooming declines.

plants.name: Rhododendron
plants.watering: Keep consistently moist but not waterlogged. Morning sun and afternoon shade ideal.
plants.fertilizing: Acidic fertilizer in spring after blooming.
plants.pruning: Right after spring bloom only. Deadhead spent flower clusters.

seasonal.spring: Blooms. Deadhead after bloom. Prune lightly if needed.
seasonal.summer: Keep moist. Mulch to retain moisture.
seasonal.winter: May need anti-desiccant spray in harsh winters.

warnings: Same old-wood blooming rules as azalea — only prune immediately after spring bloom.
Toxic to pets if ingested.

plants.name: Crape Myrtle
plants.watering: Drought tolerant once established. Water only during extended dry spells (10+ days).
plants.fertilizing: Light fertilizer in spring. Over-fertilizing produces foliage over flowers.
plants.pruning: Late winter — remove suckers from base, crossing branches, and seed heads from prior year. NEVER top.

seasonal.spring: New growth. Light pruning and cleanup.
seasonal.summer: Blooms June-September. Deadhead for second flush.
seasonal.fall: Seed heads. Leave for winter interest or remove.
seasonal.winter: Prune in late winter while dormant.

warnings: NEVER 'top' a crape myrtle (cutting the main trunks to stubs). This is called 'crape murder' and permanently disfigures the tree. Only remove suckers, crossing branches, and last year's seed pods.
Very large specimen on property — do not attempt heavy pruning without professional help.

plants.name: Japanese Maple (Grafted)
plants.watering: Same as laceleaf — water during extended dry spells.
plants.pruning: Late winter, minimal — dead or crossing branches only.

seasonal.spring: Inspect monthly for rootstock green shoots.
seasonal.winter: Prune if needed in late February.

warnings: Rootstock issue: inspect base monthly April through September. Remove ALL green shoots from the graft union immediately — the vigorous green rootstock will completely overtake the desirable purple-leafed variety within a season if not controlled.

plants.name: Ligustrum / Privet Hedge
plants.watering: Very drought tolerant. Minimal irrigation needed once established.
plants.fertilizing: Not needed. Over-fertilizing causes excessive growth requiring more trimming.
plants.pruning: Trim 2-3 times per season: late spring (after new growth hardens), midsummer, and early fall. STOP pruning by September to allow hardening before frost.

seasonal.spring: First trim after new growth hardens — late May.
seasonal.fall: Final trim no later than early September.

warnings: Stop trimming by September — late trimming stimulates tender new growth that will be damaged by frost.

plants.name: Euonymus / Japanese Holly Hedge
plants.pruning: Same schedule as Ligustrum — 3 times per season, stop by September.

seasonal.spring: Inspect for scale insects on stems.
seasonal.summer: Trim as needed. Continue scale monitoring.
seasonal.fall: Final trim by September. Treat scale if present.

warnings: Scale insects are a significant pest — look for waxy, bumpy coating on stems. Treat with horticultural oil in late winter or early spring before new growth, and again in early summer if needed.

plants.name: Nellie Stevens Holly
plants.pruning: Late February or early March. Maintain natural pyramid form — avoid shearing into unnatural shapes.

seasonal.spring: Light pruning if needed. Red berries from prior season visible.
seasonal.winter: Red berries. Prune in late winter.

warnings: Large specimen on property — consider having a certified arborist assess periodically for structural issues.
Berries toxic if ingested in large quantities.

plants.name: Sugar/Red Maple
plants.watering: Drought tolerant. Keep mowers and string trimmers away from trunk — bark damage is a leading cause of decline.
plants.pruning: Late winter while fully dormant. HIRE A CERTIFIED ARBORIST for any significant pruning.

seasonal.spring: Watch for Verticillium wilt (sudden wilting of branches).
seasonal.summer: Maintain mulch ring. Watch for stress signs.
seasonal.winter: Dormant pruning by arborist if needed.

warnings: Large trees — any significant pruning requires a certified arborist (ISA certified). Do not attempt to prune large branches yourself.
Watch for Verticillium wilt — sudden wilting of individual branches, dark streaking in wood. Contact arborist immediately if suspected.
Protect trunk from lawn equipment damage — a 4-6 foot mulch ring is essential.

plants.name: Flowering Dogwood
plants.watering: MOST drought-sensitive tree on the property. Water deeply 2-3 times per week during summer dry spells. Shallow root system suffers quickly.
plants.fertilizing: Light acidic fertilizer in spring only.
plants.pruning: Only immediately after spring bloom. Never prune in summer, fall, or winter.

seasonal.spring: Spectacular bloom. Prune lightly if needed immediately after.
seasonal.summer: Critical watering period. Mulch heavily to retain moisture.

warnings: Most drought-sensitive plant on the property — prioritize watering during dry spells.
Watch for Dogwood Anthracnose: brown leaf spots with purple halos. Treat with fungicide; improve air circulation. Can be fatal if untreated.
Wide mulch ring essential — at least to drip line. Shallow roots compete with grass.

plants.name: Nandina (Heavenly Bamboo)
plants.pruning: Late winter — cut 1/3 of stems to ground, 1/3 to mid-height, 1/3 full height for natural layered look.

seasonal.winter: Red berries. Prune in late winter.

warnings: INVASIVE SPECIES in Virginia — spreads via bird-dispersed seeds into natural areas.
Berries are TOXIC TO BIRDS — Cedar Waxwings and other birds can die from eating large quantities.
Consider replacing with native alternatives: Virginia Sweetspire (Itea virginica), Inkberry Holly (Ilex glabra), or Beautyberry (Callicarpa americana).

plants.name: Eastern Redbud Forest Pansy
plants.pruning: Immediately after blooming in spring. Remove dead wood and crossing branches.

seasonal.spring: Stunning magenta blooms on bare branches in early April before leaves emerge.
seasonal.summer: Heart-shaped purple foliage. Watch for canker.

warnings: Watch for Cytospora canker disease — sunken, discolored areas on bark with oozing. Prune out affected wood 6-8 inches below infected area with sterilized tools. Can be fatal if extensive.

plants.name: Daylily
plants.fertilizing: Balanced fertilizer in spring as growth begins.
plants.pruning: Deadhead spent individual flowers daily during bloom season. Cut flower stalks to base after all blooms on stalk are spent. Cut foliage to 4-6 inches after first hard frost.

seasonal.winter: Dormant. Clumps can be divided in fall or early spring.

warnings: TOXIC TO CATS — all parts are highly toxic to cats, causing kidney failure. Not a concern for dogs or humans.
plants.notes: Divide clumps every 3-4 years in early fall for best blooming.

plants.name: Summersweet (Clethra)
plants.pruning: Late winter if needed — remove dead wood and shape. Can cut back hard to rejuvenate.

seasonal.summer: Fragrant white/pink flower spikes July-August. Excellent for pollinators.
seasonal.fall: Yellow fall color. Seed capsules persist.

plants.notes: Native plant — excellent for pollinators and wildlife. Tolerates partial shade and moist soils.
